walkthroughs.body_html: The Pacific plate subducts beneath the Eurasian plate off northeast Japan. The Mw 9.0 Tohoku quake of 11 March 2011 triggered a tsunami that exceeded 30 m in places, killing around 18,500 people and triggering the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear meltdown. Despite the catastrophe, Japan's seismic engineering and warning systems limited the toll relative to the energy released.

The Mw 7.0 Enriquillo-Plantain Garden Fault rupture on 12 January 2010 killed approximately 220,000 people. Shallow focus, poor construction in Port-au-Prince's slums, weak governance and post-disaster cholera epidemic compounded the disaster. Recovery has been slow despite billions in international aid.

Tohoku released roughly 1,000 times more energy than Haiti yet killed far fewer people. Wealth, building codes, education and political stability determine vulnerability. Disaster risk reduction must address both hazard exposure and underlying vulnerability — the Sendai Framework (2015) emphasises this approach.
